quotes.text: The United States has to continue leading on AI innovation, but never at the expense of our jobs, our privacy, or our kids’ safety. Congress must move swiftly to set some ground rules for this new technology — putting the American people in the driver’s seat, not the White House’s favorite tech billionaires.
The widespread adoption of AI surveillance poses an unprecedented threat to the rights, dignity, and security of the American people.

Right now with AI, we have two things going on: We want to be the leaders in innovation in the world and take the promise of this technology to do amazing things, but we know we have to protect jobs, child safety. We have very real concerns that we have many legislative proposals [for]. But at this moment, we have an industry — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta — all speaking with one voice [and saying] that there is a problem, that there is a true threat to a global existence. It is a true threat that we have to solve globally.
This is not a Republican or Democratic issue. This is an American issue. And it is a global issue.

We want to be the leaders in this technology, but we want it to benefit the American people. We want to protect jobs, and protect our kids, and develop a way to harness AI for good, and protect the American people from harm.

Again, we want to be the leaders in this. But there are ways as we are working with experts and we should be here working on these solutions to answer what the companies say they want: outside regulation, outside audits of what they’re doing. That’s not just people they hire who work within their companies, but let’s have people outside evaluating what happened. We have set up agencies for this kind of review in transportation, in financial services, and this is something we need to come together as Americans to address.
